clue.text: Vessel in the heavens is high

indicators.note: in says the vessel sits inside the word for the heavens

parts.note: the sky is the heavens
a tin is a container, a vessel

explanation.surface: A ship or spacecraft up in the heavens is flying high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like altitude, but here it means smelly, as meat goes high when it turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat or game that is high smells rank, so high is a synonym of smelly.

clue.text: Composer very much for his country?

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so kind'
John Philip ... was American, so his country is the USA

explanation.surface: A composer is very fond of his native land, perhaps a patriot.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip Sousa was the American composer of marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever.

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: turn tells us to twist the letters of tail into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone arriving home first turns round and goes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' is the anagram signal here, not a reversal: the word tail is rearranged rather than read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial letter or stage is the first one, so initial is a synonym of first.

clue.text: Michigan city where buzzing instrument grips priest

indicators.note: grips says one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a kazoo is a toy instrument you hum into to make a buzz
a lama is a Buddhist priest in Tibet

explanation.surface: In some Michigan town a kazoo player has a priest in a firm grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Kalamazoo is a city in southwest Michigan, USA.

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of the word orders

parts.note: a cue is the moment, the time, to come in or act

explanation.surface: A courier is told to deliver orders and to keep to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'orders': R, E, S.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from danger is to save them, a synonym of rescue.

indicators.note: retained says the answer is kept within the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Even so, the quality of the thing has been kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and equal both describe things matched or level, as in an even score.

clue.text: Illinois city up-to date in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish, up to date in fashion
ago means in the past, as in 'long ago'

explanation.surface: A city in Illinois was modern once, back in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is the largest city in the US state of Illinois.

indicators.note: failure suggests the words collapse and must be reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A model answer given to an examiner, yet the exam is failed.
explanation.definitionFit: Exemplary behaviour is ideal, a model to copy, close in meaning to perfect.

clue.text: Clear, and build a fabricated house, finally

indicators.note: fabricated means made up or constructed, so the letters are built into a new order
finally takes only the last letter of the word house

explanation.surface: Instructions are plain: build a prefabricated house, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabricated' rearranges BUILDA into AUDIBL; 'finally' adds E from 'house'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear sound is one that can be heard plainly, so audible matches clear.
Early friction matches were sold as lucifers, and Lucifer is another name for Satan, the devil.

parts.note: to riddle with holes, as with shot, is to pepper
on means regarding, about, as in 'a book on birds'
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

explanation.surface: A puzzle about one single sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle, but it is the verb: to fill with holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy Italian-American salami, a type of sausage.

parts.note: a dose taken as a 'meal' of a chemical element, swallowed so that the gut, the alimentary canal, shows up on an X-ray

explanation.surface: A basic class that focuses on the digestive system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elementary' means made of a chemical element (barium) and 'course' is a course of a meal; the 'alimentary course' is the digestive tract.
explanation.definitionFit: Patients swallow a barium compound before an X-ray because it makes the digestive tract show up clearly.

indicators.note: of tells us the answer comes out of the letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A range of studies in paranormal psychology and language.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are a mountain range in central Europe.

clue.text: Steps taken to reverse ruling on tabloid leader at last

indicators.note: to reverse means read the word for a ruling backwards

parts.note: a law is a ruling

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word tabloid

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Steps are taken to overturn a ruling on a tabloid's editor at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' looks like measures taken, but it is dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A waltz is a ballroom dance, a set pattern of steps in triple time.

definitions.meaning: ... sauce is the tangy brown condiment
Royal ... is a famous English porcelain maker, so its plates are royal dishes

explanation.surface: Gravy is poured over the plates at a royal banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Worcester is a long-established porcelain factory in the English city of Worcester.
explanation.definitionFit: The city lends its name both to Worcestershire sauce and to Royal Worcester porcelain tableware.

parts.note: the past is history
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A student facing a history test on Beethoven's sixth symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Symphony No 6 is known as the Pastoral, evoking the countryside.

definitions.meaning: a Tommy is a British soldier, whose weapon, his gun, could playfully be said to have a boy
a scamp or rascal, said affectionately

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild exclamation and an affectionate name for a rascal; read literally, a soldier's gun's child.

clue.text: Type of spider with cross and separate back

indicators.note: back says the whole combined run of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a rood is a cross, as in a church rood screen
to part is to separate

explanation.surface: A kind of spider gets angry and splits up, then returns.
explanation.walkthrough: The single 'back' turns both words together, so the cross comes out second; the spider is named for the hinged lid on its burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapdoor spiders dig burrows sealed with a hinged lid, from which they ambush prey.

indicators.note: abstract art distorts its subject, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Being suitable is just what an abstract painter wants.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain is to relate or belong properly to something, close to being appropriate.

definitions.meaning: a Brazil is a kind of nut, so like it means tasting of nuts

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both crazy and full of the flavour of nuts, such as Brazil nuts.

clue.text: Cultivation takes up to a number of years

parts.note: till means up to, until
an age is a long period of years

explanation.surface: Farming the land takes years of patient work.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the ploughing and working of soil, the cultivation of land.

definitions.meaning: to nurse a child is to bring it up

explanation.definitionFit: To rear a child is to nurture it, and the rear is the buttocks or back part.

parts.note: something stretched is long
a fellow is a person, someone

explanation.surface: A football official finds a player who is pulling a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' suggests a football official, but it is a writer of lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, the American poet, wrote lines of verse.

clue.text: Somewhat full, it reaches close to two pints

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A jug is fairly full when the liquid gets near the two-pint mark.
explanation.definitionFit: One metric measure equals about 1.76 imperial pints, close to two.

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
to carpet someone is to scold them, and to rate is an old word for scolding

explanation.surface: Someone talks about love while standing on a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' looks like a rug, but it is the verb: to reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak formally, to make a speech.

indicators.note: manoeuvres means the letters are moved around into a new position

explanation.surface: Secret operations of the final military manoeuvres.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth means acting quietly and covertly, in secrecy.

clue.text: In August, half metamerphosed as reptiles

indicators.note: something metamorphosed has changed its form, so these letters change their order
half takes the first half of the word August

explanation.surface: In August some creatures change shape, transforming into reptiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' gives AUG from 'August'; 'metamerphosed' (sic) shuffles IN, AUG and AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Iguanas are large tropical lizards, a type of reptile.

definitions.meaning: a person or bell that rings, calling someone
a dead ... is someone's exact double

explanation.definitionFit: A bell-ringer or phone caller rings, and a lookalike is called a dead ringer.

clue.text: Speedy reaction to pressure, knight replacing queen

indicators.note: replacing says one letter group is swapped out for another in the word for pressure

parts.note: a squeeze is pressure
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A rapid response under pressure as a knight takes the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' is QU, a standard abbreviation, which N replaces in SQUEEZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneeze is a sudden involuntary reflex, a very fast reaction to irritation in the nose.
